chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about killing the swallows, or hurting them in the Sanctuary. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not kill them, for I was in the presence of Ali ibn Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), so he saw me troubling them. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O my son! Do not kill them and do not harm them, for they are not harming anything'.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically Mecca or general sacred precincts)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing or harming swallows in the Haram according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the permissibility of harming or killing swallows within the Haram based on the principle of *la dharar* (no harm), as they are considered harmless creatures. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) grounds this ruling in a personal precedent set by Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), illustrating the continuity of practical jurisprudence (*fiqh*) within the Ahl al-Bayt. It highlights the Shia emphasis on observing the specific nature of animals to determine their legal status regarding protection or culling.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj who said,

en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about killing crows and disquieting them in al-Haram (the sacred area). He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not kill them. I was with Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and he saw me troubling them. He (the Imam) said to me, ‘Do not kill them or trouble them; they do not trouble anything.’”
